subject: EdgeFabric on-prem deployment: hardware partitioning & resilience checklist
messages:
From: Priya Sharma <priya@vega-analytics.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2026 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: EdgeFabric preflight - hardware partitioning questions

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the quick intro yesterday. Our infra team ran the initial inventory and we want to validate two high-level approaches before the on-site readiness call:

1) Partitioned racks (3 racks per site) with mixed GPU and storage nodes vs dedicated GPU racks + separate storage racks.
2) PV strategy: local NVMe-backed ephemeral for model cache + remote blockstore for stateful volumes.

Can you share any red flags you typically see for Option A vs Option B with Redwood private deployments? Also attaching our fillable preflight sheet — we can populate more details if helpful.

Goal: final alignment on nodepool sizing and an acceptance checklist for the on-site engineers by Friday.

Thanks,
Priya
Ops Lead, Vega Analytics
priya@vega-analytics.com

Attachment: vega-edge-preflight-sheet.xlsx (spreadsheet, 120KB)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EdgeFabric preflight - hardware partitioning questions

Hi Priya — thanks, this is great context. High-level thoughts up front, then a short checklist we use for both options.

Short answer: both approaches are valid; trade-offs are operational simplicity vs failure isolation.

Option A (mixed racks):
- Pros: better utilization across GPU/storage; fewer rack-level dependencies for small sites.
- Cons: failure domain bigger if a rack loses networking or PDUs; scheduling needs strict node labeling to avoid noisy-neighbor compute on storage-heavy nodes.

Option B (separated racks):
- Pros: clear isolation (compute failures won't impact blockstore); easier to size storage independently for retention/IO.
- Cons: potential underutilization during low GPU demand and increased cross-rack traffic (eg: NVMe cache reads to remote blockstore).

Our pragmatic recommendation for EdgeFabric sites sized ~10-40 GPUs: prefer Option A with enforced node-taints/affinities and an NVMe tier for short-lived model cache. For larger sites (>40 GPUs) consider dedicated GPU racks (Option B) to simplify maintenance windows.

Preflight checklist (we'll walk this on the on-site call):
- Nodepool mapping: label: gpu-hot, gpu-cpu-mix, storage-block
- NVMe plan: device count per node, mountpoints, fstrim schedule
- Blockstore: replication, QoS IOPS targets, and gateway placement (co-locate 2 gateways per site)
- Network: rack-to-rack latency target < 250us, BGP/MPLS or EVPN L2 as preferred topology
- Power: PDU redundancy, predictable drain order for maintenance
- Bootstrapping: air-gapped image digest, K8s admission hooks for taints/limits

We'll attach a hardware partitioning diagram and populate the sheet with a sample nodepool mapping. I'll loop in Rishi for PV/IO sizing and Laura for rollout concerns.

Best,
Soojin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: hw-partitioning-diagram.pdf

On Mon, Apr 26, 2026 at 11:02 AM Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com> wrote:
> Our pragmatic recommendation for EdgeFabric sites sized ~10-40 GPUs: prefer Option A with enforced node-taints/affinities and an NVMe tier for short-lived model cache.

Couple of addenda from infra sizing POV:
- NVMe cache sizing rule: reserve ~25% of total model working set per rack for cache; for initial deployment assume 1TB per GPU-node for small sites. We'll validate against Vega's telemetry after canary.
- Blockstore: start with 3-way replication across 3 storage nodes, set conservative IOps throttle at launch (10–15k IOPS aggregate) and raise after burn-in.
- Eviction policies: set podPriority for real-time inference pods; aggressive image GC on storage nodes only.

Question for Laura: for a 3-rack mixed layout, do we want a deployment policy that drains entire rack for maintenance (yes/no)? If yes, we need an additional spare rack or scheduled rolling windows.

Rishi
Director, Serving Runtime

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>

Thanks team — looping back to Priya with the acceptance criteria and next steps.

Priya, summary and operational ask:
- We recommend mixed racks (Option A) for your stated site sizes. We'll apply node taints/affinities to isolate io-heavy pods and a policy to prefer intra-rack scheduling when possible.
- Acceptance criteria for on-site sign-off:
  * Nodepool mapping doc completed and onboarded to our playbook
  * NVMe device binding test: write/read baseline < 6ms for 128MB objects
  * Blockstore resiliency: simulated single-node failure with auto-recovery within 15 minutes
  * Network: validated rack-to-rack latency under 250us with <0.5% loss during sustained traffic burst

Next steps:
1) Please update the attached preflight sheet with exact node counts per rack and PV class preferences.
2) We'll produce a burn-in schedule (48–72 hours) and a maintenance blackout window recommendation.
3) On-site call: Friday 10:00 AM PT — Soojin and Rishi will join.

I'll add the burn-in schedule to the Drive link above and update the diagram with explicit rack-level spare capacity.

Best regards,
Laura Bennett
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference
